policies.n: Ordinary short tourist visitor: entry visa or advance online visa authorisation required under amended section 10. Decree 2023/147 requires online application/payment; competent or nearest mission processes it. Residence in the mission city can require consular enrolment/sticker collection; outside it, approved electronic authorisation may be followed by border biometrics and visa printing at an equipped authorised checkpoint. Obtain approval before travel; this is one sequential process, not a separate walk-up arrival visa. Passport at least six months, return/onward arrangements, accommodation and sufficient means. Six-month short-stay visa validity is not an established permitted stay. Treaty/document exceptions are separately unresolved.
policies.label: Advance online visa approval

policies.n: Visa required under the embassy’s explicit rule for nationalities outside its ordinary exemption list. Passport at least six months; mission application requires travel and accommodation/invitation evidence. The precise electronic, consular or airport issuance method and permitted stay are not established by this source. This rule does not claim eVisa or visa on arrival is unavailable.
policies.label: Visa required; issuance method unconfirmed

policies.n: Tourist visa required for a regular Canadian passport. Permitted stay and electronic/arrival eligibility are not established; no claim that an electronic method is unavailable.

German citizens require an entry visa. Berlin tourist procedure requires tourism-agency invitation or sponsor approval from Sudanese authorities before mission issuance. Permitted stay is unspecified; an online form is not proof of end-to-end eVisa issuance.

Serbian national passport requires a visa; MFA describes competent-mission issuance following a Sudanese host’s prior authority request. Current stay and alternative electronic/arrival eligibility are not established.
Ordinary Serbian passport exemption for stays up to 30 days.
French tourist exemption; passport valid at least six months, return ticket and hotel reservation. Paid activity needs separate permission.
MEA explicitly lists ordinary Indian passports for visa-free entry for 90 days. No third-country visa/residence condition is attached to this row.
Free tourist visa issued on arrival to Canadian ordinary-passport holders. Maximum 90 days, continuous or divided among visits, within 180 days from first entry; not 90 fresh days on every entry.
Singapore passport exemption for up to 90 days within a 180-day period. The source warns that passports bearing only a single name are not accepted. No assumption of unlimited repeat 90-day stays.
Serbian ordinary national passports are visa-exempt for stays up to 90 days under the bilateral agreement. The source does not specify a rolling/aggregate 180-day period; no such period is inferred.

Kosovo ordinary passports are explicitly exempt from entry visa requirements; current MOFA inbound list corroborates the exemption. UAE-bound stay duration is unspecified. The treaty notice’s 90 days per visit refers to UAE citizens entering Kosovo and is not reversed.

Taiwan is expressly visa-required in the regular-passport column of the UAE mission’s public table. Tourist visas are arranged through UAE visa agents/hotels or a sponsor, with a copy obtained before travel. No unrestricted personal eVisa or stay length is proved.
policies.label: Advance visa via sponsor or agent

policies.n: The nationality-specific diplomatic/official/service concessions do not cover ordinary tourist passports. Obtain a consular visa or prior General Security approval under article 11. No ordinary-passport waiver or unrestricted arrival entitlement is asserted. Permitted stay and any electronic channel remain unconfirmed.

Visa requirement established, but arrival versus prior-approval scope remains uncertain: article 8 describes an airport visa for one month, extendable to three, with non-refundable round-trip ticket, accommodation/contact and USD 2,000 cash or certified cheque; article 10 addresses female nationals and prior General Security tourism approval. Do not assume eligibility for walk-up issuance. A pre-issued consular visa/prior approval is the documented route to clarify with the authority; d=0 does not transfer the airport duration to every method.
policies.label: Visa required; arrival eligibility needs confirmation

policies.n: HKSAR passports of all ages must obtain Kenya eTA before travel. This is specific to HKSAR passports, not BN(O) or Hong Kong identity documents. The cited Kenya remark gives no permitted stay.

Short tourist visa exemption is established. French guidance says less than three months; Barbados’s current France row contains conflicting three-in-six-month and six-month limits. Maximum allowance remains unresolved, so no numerical day count or six-month entitlement is asserted.
policies.label: Visa-free short visit; maximum stay disputed

policies.n: Taiwan ordinary passports only; not diplomatic/official. Fourteen-day stay is non-extendable and cannot be converted to another visa category. Passport valid six months beyond intended stay, accommodation, financial capacity, return/onward ticket and no derogatory Immigration record required. Complete free eTravel arrival declaration within 72 hours before arrival. For more than fourteen days or permit-requiring activities, obtain the relevant visa beforehand. MECO states no expiry date.

findings: Recovered Sudan’s official Arabic 1994 Passport and Immigration Act through the Ministry of Justice’s public e-book manifest. Publication metadata is 2017-05-01; section 10(1) requires entry visas, but 10(4), 13 and 27 expressly empower nationality/class/personal exemptions. These unreconciled presidential and ministerial orders prevent a worldwide default expansion.

Berlin’s actual tourist page and linked Arabic requirements document, The Hague’s entry-visa page, Canadian/German/Serbian ordinary-nationality advice inspected. Added only CA/DE/RS from explicit nationality evidence; sponsor/online-form processing is not relabelled eVisa.

All remaining assigned origins: current exemption orders and ordinary-nationality/age/sex/routing schedules still unproved. EG/KW/AE/YE and CN/ER/KE/MY/QA need their claimed special regimes; IL needs current admission evidence; HK/MO/PS/TW/XK need document handling. No country-list dropdown is proof.

Fresh signed Law 2022/015 page 2 and all 21 pages of Decree 2023/147 inspected. Section 10 supplies the temporary-visitor visa/online-authorisation default; decree articles 28–35 supply the actual electronic workflow. Current Brussels and London instructions corroborate its continued operation. Statutory default, not omission from a list, supports 176 additions.

CF/CG/GA/GQ/TD: CEMAC exemption and current document implementation remain unresolved. ML/NG: reported ordinary bilateral exceptions require operative nationality evidence. All seven withheld from the statutory default. HK/MO/PS/TW/XK: recognition-specific cases withheld.

The 2023 decree preserves agreement/convention fee provisions and repeals inconsistent 2007/2008/2016 implementation provisions. No fee waiver is treated as visa exemption, no six-month validity is converted into stay, and electronic authorisation plus border printing is not encoded as alternative methods.

DGSN documentation returned 404/500; public CEMAC search yielded no operative schedule. Official eVisa FAQ still returns an application error. Additional Belgium/Germany/Italy/Ottawa/London mission and Presidency searches are cached.

Reviewed every assigned origin against the freshly retrieved ministry exemption PDF. It still omits many known waivers and supplies no explicit complement/default. Added only the individually evidenced IN90, RS30 and FR3-month exemptions.

Brussels mission’s short-stay update, EEAS travel page and linked FAQ retrieved. They describe Trinidadians entering Europe; they are not silently reversed to establish all EU passports entering Trinidad. EUR-Lex treaty endpoints returned empty 202 responses; Council returned 403.

All remaining assigned origins: actual current incoming ordinary nationality schedule/operative bilateral text not retrieved. Ministry eVisa availability alone is not evidence that every omitted nationality requires a visa. Law-library TLS/404 failures and incomplete tourism/mission material retained.

Brussels embassy supplies a full positive list plus an explicit unlisted-nationality visa-required sentence. This resolves the requirement for 131 ordinary-nationality gaps. Issuance methods and stay remain unconfirmed, not assumed consular-only.

CH remains unresolved because a Swiss waiver is reported but Brussels omits it; no negative rule assigned amid that concrete exception concern. HK/MO/PS/TW/XK remain document-specific gaps rather than being treated as mainland China or an unrecognised-code default.

Fresh New York/Brussels missions inspected. London live hostname fails DNS. Wayback 2024 capture is a verification page; 2022-07-03 capture is real and links a 2017 nationality PDF, but the PDF is not archived/retrievable (404). No historical nationality rule is claimed from that link alone.

CA90-on-arrival with first-entry 180-day aggregate; SG90/180 exemption; RS90 exemption with no invented rolling period; XK exemption with unknown inbound stay; TW explicit regular-column prior-visa rule newly supported.

MOFA Kosovo notice gives 90 days only in the UAE-to-Kosovo direction. Current inbound schedule corroborates Kosovo exemption but not its duration. Washington table’s explicit Taiwan regular-passport result resolves the previously absent MOFA card.

All remaining assigned origins: general Visa Free cards and embassy arrival-language do not settle nationality-specific waiver versus arrival issuance, passport subtype, or 30/90/180 conditions. An inspected Sharjah 2025 guide says 30 days even for US/UK/EU, conflicting with more specific current 90-day sources; it is rejected for broad expansion.

London recovered visa-information page redirects guidance to now-missing u.ae routes. Canberra/Tokyo/Mexico, GDRFA, tourism-authority, official-airport and origin-government leads were pursued; access failures/challenges and wrong-destination redirects were not treated as evidence.

Arabic and English full nationality provisions inspected. CO/CU/KZ special-passport concessions do not apply to ordinary tourism; prior-visa/approval default retained. EG/GH common visa requirement recorded without pretending the conflicting arrival/prior-authorisation clauses are resolved.

CD/UG: explicit suspension concerns new visa issuance, not a proven nationality-wide admission ban; existing permission and current ordinary-tourist handling still unresolved. IL/XK: accepted-document/admission rule not established. PS: Jordanian/Palestinian documents and routing-specific approval need differentiation. SY: distinct Syrian-entry regime remains unproved for general tourism. TR: free-arrival-visa versus Turkish-MFA waiver conflict persists.

No nationality-wide ban is created from labour-recruitment restrictions, nor a visa exemption from zero fees. Ghana-specific page confirms residence/work limits but does not independently settle the article 8/10 arrival issue.

All nine gaps rechecked against fresh September-linked central guidelines and Abuja mission material. Section 6 exempts Commonwealth countries except six named states; section 7 separately lists CM/FJ/GA/MV/NG/LK/TG for online/arrival visas. The contradiction remains, even though Abuja specifically describes Nigerian tourist visa fees and stays.

NI is still not clearly assigned in the current schedules; TW accepted ordinary-passport procedure is not established. No omission/default or “all Commonwealth” expansion, and no old mission referral list is presented as current central policy.
HK resolved from Hong Kong Immigration’s Kenya-specific eTA remark, corroborating the Kenyan portal and expressly identifying HKSAR passports of all ages.

SO: current Kenyan eTA page names six EAC partners but not Somalia, while regional wording is broader; implementation remains unresolved. XK/MO/PS/TW: specific document/checker outcome not obtained. General eTA wording and a nationality selector are insufficient.
FR common short-visit exemption recorded with d=0 because both official sources agree on exemption but not its maximum. No six-month claim and no conversion of months to 90 days.

Fresh 9 May 2025 schedule retains blank MV/TL inbound cells and lacks PS; Immigration still links an older 2022 schedule. Maldives MFA returned 403. All three remain unresolved; outbound columns and blanks are not inverted.

MECO’s current Taiwan-specific service and detailed FAQ explicitly support ordinary-passport vf14, non-extendable/non-convertible, with supporting documents and eTravel. This is more specific operational guidance than the older conflicting Washington sheet; no unsupported expiry inferred.

ME/SS: no individually named current incoming entry rule obtained. Montenegro page describes Filipinos entering Montenegro, so not reversed; Budapest/Nairobi Philippine mission retrievals returned 403. No inference from missing names on the 157-country chart.

Both XK and PS researched through Ankara/Amman/Tel Aviv/Cairo/New Delhi visa-service routes and the public Thai eVisa FAQ. Retrieved pages were generic navigation/service shells, and did not substantiate accepted ordinary documents and a nationality-specific competent-mission tourist pathway.
The baseline visa obligation is not converted into a standard eVisa or admission ban without resolving the special-document handling. Both remain unresolved.

Fresh Finnish MFA Somalia-specific document page explicitly accepts the Somali biometric DIPLOMATIC ePassport introduced in 2014 and states visa required. It does not accept the ordinary passport or document a tourist substitute/LTV pathway. SO remains unresolved, not a nationality-wide ban.

Fresh SEM nationality PDF, dated 3 April 2026, and its linked national-document framework inspected. Somalia remains visa-required with document qualification; Swiss mission page returned 403. A current ordinary-tourist separate-sheet/substitute-document issuance pathway is still not established. SO remains unresolved.

IL remains unresolved: actual Israeli ordinary-passport treaty/waiver document not obtained; government PDF returned 403 and Nauru MFA/alternate government hostnames failed DNS. Prior tourism fee waiver is not a visa waiver. No absence-based visa requirement or admission prohibition added.
